I have had 3 of these elements in my Electrolux dryer in the last 6 years (including the one it came with).  The main reason I have had to replace the element is 2-fold:  (1) I was using flexible dryer duct that traveled around 20 feet before exiting the house.  As you may know, flexible duct is horrible at collecting lint in the folds and won't fully clean out even if you use a leaf-blower.  This likely sped up the process of the element overheating.  However, the other reason is (2) The design of the element allows the inner partition of the element to warp and eventually touch the outer sides of the canister, causing a ground condition and basically killing your element.  Had they designed this thing a little better, the element wouldn't warp and wouldn't cause a ground-out even if the dryer was getting a bit too hot.  Considering how much these things cost, that's a big deal.  So, to summarize, install solid ductwork (cheap and easy, so no excuses!).  Second, realize that over time, your element will warp and eventually fail unless they change the design (not likely). B-minus....

This is an quality OEM heating element and an exact replacement and fit for Electrolux MODEL  EIED55HIW dryer.  This dryer is very easy for a DIY to repair.  To replace the element all you have to do is remove the top panel, control panel, and the front panel/door.  Then the element can be seen in the lower left corner.  Mark where each wire goes onto the element.  Once element is removed, you need to exchange the sensors and mounting legs from the old element and install them on the new element.  Total job should take less then 1 hour.  A very good step by step video on disassemble of this dryer can be found on YouTube.  Search for this video in the YouTube search box ' ornFxw2D7yk '

This heating element fixed our Electrolux electric dryer error E64. We installed it in less than 2 hours thanks to the help of YouTube and google searches. It took about 40 minutes to remove the top/back panels and remove the old element, and less time to mount the new unit and re install the brackets and wiring (5 wires, all plug or bolt on). According to others, this is a common point of failure for this type of dryer. A service call to repair the issue was going to be at least $500. We have 0 experience repairing appliances and all the tools that were needed are a Philips head screwdriver of varying lengths and a pair of channel locks/pliers, but a screw gun makes it faster.
My husband was able to install this part which saved us a lot of money in repair cost.
